how_tested: One request at a time, 1.2 to 1.6 seconds apart, at most three per site, User-Agent 'congress-catalog/1.0 (personal legislative research; thecivicarchive.github.io)'. Feeds were found from each home page's own <link rel=alternate> tags, then from patterns the same publishing system uses (WordPress /feed/, NPR Grove <section>.rss, Arc /arc/outboundfeeds/rss/?outputType=xml, BLOX /search/?f=rss). Nothing from any feed item was stored.
reuse_rule: Show the headline, the outlet's name, the time and a link to the story. Never copy the summary or article text, even where the feed carries it (feed_carries_full_text). States Newsroom outlets license republication (CC BY-ND 4.0) but we still link rather than copy.

gdelt.credit_required: Any use or redistribution must cite the GDELT Project and link to https://www.gdeltproject.org/ (About page, Terms of Use, checked 2026-10-09). Use is otherwise unrestricted, free, no key.

raw_files.what: A three-line text file, rewritten every 15 minutes: size, MD5 and address of the newest export (events), mentions and gkg zip files, named by UTC time (e.g. 20261010031500.gkg.csv.zip).
raw_files.tested: 2026-10-09: list answered 200; the gkg file of 03:15 UTC was 2.6 MB zipped, 571 articles (155 distinct sources), 73 election-themed, 40 of them with a US location; every row carried a <PAGE_TITLE>. About 250 MB a day; an election night (18:00 to 06:00) about 125 MB.

gkg_columns_used.11/12: V2Persons (names found in the text; matched to candidates, never stored apart from the match)

raw_files.location_types: 1 country, 2 US state, 3 US city or landmark, 4 world city, 5 world state. ADM1 'USMN' = Minnesota; ADM2 'NY067' = state postal code + county FIPS (Onondaga, 36067); featureID of a US city is its GNIS id, which the Census place files carry as the ANSI code.
raw_files.known_error: Seen in the test file: an article from courierherald.com (Enumclaw, Washington State) about Washington State voters was placed at 'Washington, Washington' = the White House, DC. City-level GDELT places are therefore medium confidence at best and are checked against the outlet's home state.
raw_files.plan: The updater fetches lastupdate.txt every 15 minutes, downloads the new gkg zip once (MD5 checked), keeps rows whose V2Themes include ELECTION or TAX_FNCACT_CANDIDATE and whose V2Locations or source is in the US, and stores url, outlet, time, title, matched race ids and places. Nothing else is kept.

doc_api.documented: query (keywords, "phrases", OR in (), sourcecountry:US, sourcelang:english, domain:, theme:ELECTION, near:), mode=artlist (up to maxrecords=250 articles), timelinevol, timelinevolraw (counts per 15 minutes), timelinesourcecountry, tonechart; format=json|rss|csv; timespan=15min..3months or startdatetime/enddatetime; sort=datedesc. Updated every 15 minutes. Limit: one request every 5 seconds (stated in its own 429 reply).
doc_api.tested: 2026-10-09: nine requests, 5 to 45 seconds apart: seven answered 429, two answered 200 with an empty {} (no articles). Not usable from this machine today; the raw files above give the same articles and are the plan. Retry once on a quiet day before relying on it even for backfill.

gdelt.ngrams: GDELT's 429 reply points heavy users to its Web News NGrams 3.0 dataset (blog.gdeltproject.org); not needed at our volume.

jetstream.filters: wantedCollections (app.bsky.feed.post for posts; leave out reposts and likes), wantedDids (only these accounts: used for the official-account stream), cursor=<time_us> to resume after a drop, compress=true for zstd (needs a dictionary; not needed at our volume).
jetstream.tested: 2026-10-09 22:20 CT, 30 seconds, standard library only (no package installed): handshake 101; 891 new posts (29.7 a second), 0.03 MB a second uncompressed; 65% English; 3 posts said 'election', 5 'vote'. Event keys: did, kind, time_us, commit{operation, collection, rkey, record, cid, rev}; kinds commit, account, identity.
jetstream.software: Jetstream v2 is replacing v1 at the same addresses with the same JSON (github.com/bluesky-social/jetstream docs/README.md, read 2026-10-09); MIT or Apache-2.0.
jetstream.counting_without_identities: Match each post's text against each race's keyword set in memory. Add 1 to a per-race, per-minute counter. For 'distinct people' use an HMAC of the did with a salt made at start and never written; keep the set only for the current hour, then keep just its size. Never write a did, handle, text or post id of an ordinary account to disk or log.
jetstream.official_stream: A second connection with wantedDids = the checked official accounts (up to the server's limit; Jetstream v1 documented 10,000). These posts may be stored and shown: text, time, link to the post, account name.
jetstream.deletion_duty: Bluesky Developer Guidelines (bsky.network/docs/developer-guidelines, read 2026-10-09): 'All services must have a method for deleting content a user has requested to be deleted.' On a delete commit for a shown post, remove it; on an account event with active=false, hide that account's posts. Also: a way to report content, a public contact address that is read, reasonable security.

bluesky.official_accounts: Verified when (a) the handle is the organization's own domain (mprnews.org, startribune.com, npr.org, apnews.com are), or (b) the organization's own website (the address in our tables) links to bsky.app/profile/<handle>, and the profile names the same organization; Bluesky's blue check (verification.verifiedStatus) is a supporting sign only: the search for 'Secretary of State' returned verified UK MPs and only one US election office (oregonsos.bsky.social), and no .gov handles.

mastodon.rate_limit: Headers on every reply: x-ratelimit-limit 300 per 5 minutes per IP per instance (checked 2026-10-09). Planned use: 6 tags x 7 instances every 3 minutes = 14 requests a minute across all instances.
mastodon.terms: mastodon.social terms (effective 2026-08-31, via /api/v1/instance/terms_of_service): content is public and 'Anyone, or any computer, might access your Content via RSS aggregators and readers ... or index and store your Content in search engines and databases.'
mastodon.privacy_flags: Each status carries account.indexable (opted in to search), account.discoverable, account.bot. Count only posts whose account is indexable or discoverable and not a bot; skip any account whose note contains #nobot. Never store the account.
mastodon.dedupe: The same post reaches several instances; dedupe by status.uri.
mastodon.official: account.fields[].verified_at is set when the linked website links back (rel=me); an official account is one whose verified field is the organization's or campaign's own domain from our tables.
mastodon.tags: #election, #elections, #election2026, #midterms, #vote, plus each state's own (#mnpol, #mnleg, #wipolitics ...) chosen by looking, never guessed into the counts unadjusted.

official_accounts_plan.method: Fetch each official website once (polite, cached), read only links to bsky.app/profile/, mastodon @-profiles and youtube channels; accept an account only with two anchors: the site links to it AND the account points back (Bluesky handle = the site's domain, or profile text/link naming the domain; Mastodon verified_at field; YouTube channel 'About' link). Store the account, the page that links it and the date. No guessing from names.
official_accounts_plan.sample: 24 campaign sites read 2026-10-09 (12 Minnesota local, 12 federal): Facebook 20, Instagram 15, X 10, YouTube 4, Bluesky 3, Mastodon 3, Threads 1; none used rel=me. Most candidates' official posts are on networks we do not read (X, Facebook, Instagram), so the shown stream will be mostly newsrooms and election offices; the page should say so.

measures.window: Rolling 60 minutes on election night (24 hours before it), recomputed every 5 minutes. A race's mentions = news items (RSS + GDELT, deduplicated) and social mentions (Bluesky + Mastodon distinct people) kept as separate numbers.
news_item_rules: One story = one canonical URL (strip query strings and AMP); the same headline from several outlets (wire copy) counts once per outlet.
Per-outlet cap: at most 3 items per race per window.
An aggregator (RealClearPolitics) counts as the outlet it links to, not itself.

coverage_per_100k.formula: raw = 100000 * N / pop; shown = 100000 * (N + m * R_level) / (pop + m * 100000)
coverage_per_100k.terms: N = capped news items in the window; pop = residents of the race's area from ACS 2020-2024 5-year table B01003 (already cached in states_cache/acs2024; summary levels 040 state, 500 congressional district, 610/620 legislative districts, 050 county, 060 county subdivision, 160 place, 950/960/970 school districts; multi-county districts add their counties); R_level = all items / all residents (per 100,000) for races of the same level; m = 1 (the prior is worth 100,000 residents).
coverage_per_100k.why_shrink: A school board of 5,000 people with 2 stories would score 40 per 100,000 raw and top the board; shrunk toward its level's average it scores about 2 + R_level. The raw figure is still shown beside it.
coverage_per_100k.ranked_when: N >= 3 from >= 2 outlets in the window; boards are kept per level (statewide, Congress, legislature, county, city and school), never one board for all.

attention_gap.formula: gap = pct_rank(closeness) - pct_rank(coverage_per_100k), within the level; closeness = 1 - |margin|
attention_gap.margin: Live: (leader - runner-up) / (their combined votes), used once at least 20% of the expected vote is counted; before that the forecast median margin from the predictions section; a race with neither is not ranked.
attention_gap.reading: From -100 to +100 points. Large positive = closer than its coverage suggests (an under-covered close race); large negative = much covered, not close. Includes races with zero coverage, which is the point.
attention_gap.guard: Retention and unopposed races are left out; a race's margin source (live or forecast) is printed beside the figure.

momentum.formula: momentum = (c_last + 1) / (c_prev + 1), c = news items + social distinct people in the last 60 minutes and the 60 before
momentum.rising_test: Shown as 'rising' only when c_last exceeds the upper 95% Poisson bound of c_prev (so 3 -> 6 is noise, 30 -> 60 is not).
momentum.viral_guard: Social counts are distinct people, not posts; each person counts once per race per hour; reposts are not read; one news story counts once per outlet.

source_breadth.formula: distinct = number of distinct outlets (registered domain) with an item on the race in the last 24 hours; effective = exp(-sum p_o ln p_o), p_o = outlet o's share of the race's items
source_breadth.reading: The effective number falls when one outlet writes most of the stories (10 items, 8 from one paper: distinct 3, effective about 1.9).

measures.large_market_guard: Per-100,000 shrinkage, per-level boards, per-outlet caps and distinct-people social counts. National outlets are counted like any other outlet, so a Senate race does not win by being national: it is ranked only against other statewide races.

order.rule: Race match: the headline names a candidate on that race's list (full name, or family name with the office or district words) and the outlet's home state or the headline's state names the race's state

Place name in the headline matched to sl_places / Census names with a state context (outlet home state or a state named in the headline); ambiguous names (Washington, Springfield, 'Jackson County') need the state
order.confidence: high when one match in the state, otherwise not placed

order.rule: GDELT V2Locations: the most-mentioned US location of type 2 or 3 that agrees with the outlet's home state
order.places_at: state (type 2) or county via ADM2 / place via GNIS id (type 3)
order.confidence: medium (low when it disagrees with the outlet's home state: the Enumclaw example)

order.rule: Outlet home market (feeds[].market, state for statewide outlets)
order.confidence: low; marked 'placed by where the outlet is'

order.places_at: only through a race or place match in the text; never from any user's location

geotagging.display: Each item on the map carries its confidence and the rule that placed it; low-confidence items appear only at state zoom.

privacy: No personal contact details were printed or stored. Feed items were counted, not kept. No did, handle or account of an ordinary Bluesky or Mastodon user was printed or stored; the Jetstream test kept only totals.
